                      fig.width = 5.5, fig.height = 3.4)

```{r compute}
# values quoted in the notes; same seeds and settings as the R demos in
# CODE_Week10_ModelComparison.R
library(emdbook)
library(MASS)
library(glmnet)

fir <- na.omit(FirDBHFec[, c("TOTCONES", "DBH", "WAVE_NON")])
fir$TOTCONES <- round(fir$TOTCONES)
wave <- as.numeric(fir$WAVE_NON)
nll_nb <- function(a, b, k) {
  -sum(dnbinom(fir$TOTCONES, mu = a * fir$DBH^b, size = k, log = TRUE))
}
nll_full <- function(p) nll_nb(p[1:2][wave], p[3:4][wave], p[5:6][wave])
nll_nowave <- function(p) nll_nb(p[1], p[2], p[3])
nll_constb <- function(p) nll_nb(p[1:2][wave], p[3], p[4:5][wave])
nll_constak <- function(p) nll_nb(p[1], p[2:3][wave], p[4])
nll_pois <- function(p) -sum(dpois(fir$TOTCONES, p[1] * fir$DBH^p[2], log = TRUE))
fit_model <- function(nll, start) {
  fit <- optim(start, nll, control = list(maxit = 10000))
  optim(fit$par, nll, method = "BFGS", control = list(maxit = 10000))
}
fit_full <- fit_model(nll_full, c(1, 1, 2, 2, 1, 1))
fit_nowave <- fit_model(nll_nowave, c(1, 2, 1))
fit_constb <- fit_model(nll_constb, c(1, 1, 2, 1, 1))
fit_constak <- fit_model(nll_constak, c(1, 2, 2, 1))
fit_pois <- fit_model(nll_pois, c(1, 2))
lrt_dev <- 2 * (fit_nowave$value - fit_full$value)
lrt_p <- pchisq(lrt_dev, df = 3, lower.tail = FALSE)
pois_dev <- 2 * (fit_pois$value - fit_nowave$value)

fits <- list(full = fit_full, const_b = fit_constb, const_ak = fit_constak,
             no_wave = fit_nowave, poisson = fit_pois)
n_fir <- nrow(fir)
aic_tab <- data.frame(model = names(fits),
                      k = sapply(fits, function(f) length(f$par)),
                      nll = sapply(fits, function(f) f$value))
aic_tab$AIC <- 2 * aic_tab$nll + 2 * aic_tab$k
aic_tab$dAIC <- aic_tab$AIC - min(aic_tab$AIC)
aic_tab$weight <- exp(-aic_tab$dAIC / 2) / sum(exp(-aic_tab$dAIC / 2))
aic_tab$AICc <- aic_tab$AIC + 2 * aic_tab$k * (aic_tab$k + 1) / (n_fir - aic_tab$k - 1)
aic_tab$BIC <- 2 * aic_tab$nll + log(n_fir) * aic_tab$k
aic_tab <- aic_tab[order(aic_tab$AIC), ]
rownames(aic_tab) <- aic_tab$model
bic_d <- aic_tab$BIC - min(aic_tab$BIC)
names(bic_d) <- aic_tab$model

covars <- c("canopy", "big_trees", "snags", "shrub", "elev", "slope",
            "north", "road_dist", "stream_dist", "grazing")
beta_true <- c(0, 0.5, 0.4, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0.3, 0, 0)
cov_mat <- diag(10)
cov_mat[1, 2] <- cov_mat[2, 1] <- 0.6
cov_mat[1, 4] <- cov_mat[4, 1] <- -0.4
cov_mat[5, 6] <- cov_mat[6, 5] <- 0.5
set.seed(19)
X <- mvrnorm(50, rep(0, 10), cov_mat)
colnames(X) <- covars
creepers <- rpois(50, exp(log(2) + X %*% beta_true))
fit_glm <- glm(creepers ~ X, family = poisson)
b_mle <- setNames(coef(fit_glm)[-1], covars)
subsets <- expand.grid(rep(list(c(FALSE, TRUE)), 10))
subset_aic <- apply(subsets, 1, function(use) {
  if (!any(use)) return(AIC(glm(creepers ~ 1, family = poisson)))
  AIC(glm(creepers ~ X[, use, drop = FALSE], family = poisson))
})
best_set <- covars[unlist(subsets[which.min(subset_aic), ])]
n_within2 <- sum(subset_aic - min(subset_aic) < 2)
subset_wt <- exp(-(subset_aic - min(subset_aic)) / 2)
best_wt <- max(subset_wt) / sum(subset_wt)
# top-models table: rank and dAIC of the true model; how many top models are the
# best model plus one extra covariate
subset_rank <- order(subset_aic)
true_rows <- which(apply(subsets, 1, function(use) all(use == (beta_true != 0))))
true_rank <- match(true_rows, subset_rank)
true_daic <- subset_aic[true_rows] - min(subset_aic)
best_use <- unlist(subsets[subset_rank[1], ])
plus_one <- sapply(subset_rank[2:10], function(r) {
  use <- unlist(subsets[r, ])
  sum(use) == sum(best_use) + 1 && all(use[best_use])
})
plus_one_daic <- (subset_aic[subset_rank[2:10]] - min(subset_aic))[plus_one]
fit_ridge <- glmnet(X, creepers, family = "poisson", alpha = 0)
fit_lasso <- glmnet(X, creepers, family = "poisson", alpha = 1)
set.seed(746)
cv_lasso <- cv.glmnet(X, creepers, family = "poisson", alpha = 1)
b_lasso <- setNames(coef(cv_lasso, s = "lambda.1se")[-1], covars)
set.seed(746)
cv_ridge <- cv.glmnet(X, creepers, family = "poisson", alpha = 0)
b_ridge <- setNames(coef(cv_ridge, s = "lambda.1se")[-1], covars)
b_ridge_min <- setNames(coef(cv_ridge, s = "lambda.min")[-1], covars)
lasso_set <- covars[b_lasso != 0]

f2 <- function(v) formatC(v, format = "f", digits = 2)
f1 <- function(v) formatC(v, format = "f", digits = 1)
lst <- function(v) paste(gsub("_", "\\\\_", v), collapse = ", ")
```

```{r tally, cache=TRUE}
# how often does each method recover the true set, across 40 datasets like the creeper one?
tally <- t(sapply(1:40, function(s) {
  set.seed(s)
  Xs <- mvrnorm(50, rep(0, 10), cov_mat)
  ys <- rpois(50, exp(log(2) + Xs %*% beta_true))
  aics <- apply(subsets, 1, function(use) {
    if (!any(use)) return(AIC(glm(ys ~ 1, family = poisson)))
    AIC(glm(ys ~ Xs[, use, drop = FALSE], family = poisson))
  })
  cvs <- cv.glmnet(Xs, ys, family = "poisson", alpha = 1)
  truth <- beta_true != 0
  c(aic = all(unlist(subsets[which.min(aics), ]) == truth),
    lasso = all((coef(cvs, s = "lambda.1se")[-1] != 0) == truth))
}))
n_aic_right <- sum(tally[, "aic"])
n_lasso_right <- sum(tally[, "lasso"])
```

```{r sketch-helpers}
# scientific workflow schematic; 'highlight' shades one box (e.g. "COMPARE")
draw_workflow <- function(highlight = NULL, cex = 0.8) {
  boxes <- c("PROBLEM", "THEORIES", "MODELS", "FIT", "COMPARE")
  subs <- c("what do we\nneed to know?", "candidate\nexplanations",
            "data-generating\n(process + noise)", "confront each\nwith data",
            "fit, prediction,\nrelevance")
  x <- seq(1, 9, by = 2)
  y <- 2
  w <- 0.8
  h <- 0.55
  shade <- function(lab) if (!is.null(highlight) && lab == highlight) "grey80" else "white"
  par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
  plot(NA, xlim = c(0, 10), ylim = c(-0.2, 4), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
  for (i in seq_along(boxes)) {
    rect(x[i] - w, y - h, x[i] + w, y + h, col = shade(boxes[i]), lwd = 1.5)
    text(x[i], y + 0.18, boxes[i], font = 2, cex = cex)
    text(x[i], y - 0.22, subs[i], cex = cex * 0.75)
  }
  arrows(x[-5] + w, y, x[-1] - w, y, length = 0.08, lwd = 1.5)
  rect(6 - 0.7, 3.2 - 0.35, 6 + 0.7, 3.2 + 0.35, col = shade("DATA"), lty = 2, lwd = 1.5)
  text(6, 3.28, "DATA", font = 2, cex = cex)
  text(6, 3.0, "study design", cex = cex * 0.75)
  arrows(x[3], y + h, 6 - 0.7, 3.2, length = 0.08, lty = 2, lwd = 1.2)
  arrows(6 + 0.7, 3.2, x[4], y + h, length = 0.08, lty = 2, lwd = 1.2)
  segments(x[5], y - h, x[5], 0.4, lwd = 1.5)
  segments(x[5], 0.4, x[1], 0.4, lwd = 1.5)
  arrows(x[c(1, 2)], 0.4, x[c(1, 2)], y - h, length = 0.08, lwd = 1.5)
  text(6, 0.15, "REVISE the problem and theories; drop or down-weight poor models",
       cex = cex * 0.85, font = 3)
}

# WOD figure: least-squares line, a curve through every point, and the new plot
wod_x <- c(3, 8, 10, 14, 25, 27, 32)
wod_y <- c(7, 8, 15, 9.5, 18, 16, 20.5)
wod_line <- lm(wod_y ~ wod_x)
wod_curve <- splinefun(wod_x, wod_y, method = "natural")
wod_pred <- c(line = unname(predict(wod_line, data.frame(wod_x = 19))), curve = wod_curve(19))
draw_wod <- function() {
  par(mar = c(3, 3, 0.5, 0.5), mgp = c(1.8, 0.5, 0))
  plot(wod_x, wod_y, pch = 19, xlim = c(0, 35), ylim = c(0, 25), xaxs = "i", yaxs = "i",
       xlab = "Soil moisture (%)", ylab = "Height (cm)")
  abline(v = 19, lty = 3, col = "grey50")
  abline(wod_line, lwd = 2)
  xs <- seq(2, 33, 0.1)
  lines(xs, pmin(wod_curve(xs), 25), lwd = 2, lty = 2)
  points(19, 14, pch = 4, cex = 1.5, lwd = 2.5)
}

# chi-square(3) density with the 95% cutoff and the fir deviance
draw_chisq <- function() {
  par(mar = c(3, 3, 0.5, 0.5), mgp = c(1.8, 0.5, 0))
  curve(dchisq(x, 3), 0, 12, lwd = 2, xlab = "Deviance", ylab = "Density",
        ylim = c(0, 0.33))
  abline(v = qchisq(0.95, 3), lty = 2)
  abline(v = lrt_dev, lwd = 3, col = "grey40")
  text(qchisq(0.95, 3), 0.29, "95% cutoff: 7.81", pos = 4, cex = 0.8)
  text(lrt_dev, 0.29, paste0("fir: ", f2(lrt_dev)), pos = 4, cex = 0.8)
}

# one coefficient: NLL = (beta - 0.3)^2, alone and with a ridge or lasso penalty
draw_penalty_1d <- function() {
  par(mar = c(3, 3, 0.5, 10), mgp = c(1.8, 0.5, 0))
  b <- seq(-0.3, 0.6, length.out = 500)
  nll <- (b - 0.3)^2
  ridge <- nll + 1 * b^2
  lasso <- nll + 0.8 * abs(b)
  plot(b, lasso, type = "l", lwd = 2, lty = 2, ylim = c(0, 0.45),
       xlab = "Coefficient", ylab = "penalized NLL")
  lines(b, ridge, lwd = 2, lty = 3)
  lines(b, nll, lwd = 2)
  abline(v = 0, col = "grey70")
  points(c(0.3, 0.15, 0), c(0, (0.15 - 0.3)^2 + 0.15^2, 0.09), pch = 19)
  legend("right", c("NLL alone\n(min 0.30)", "+ ridge\n(min 0.15)", "+ lasso\n(min exactly 0)"),
         lwd = 2, lty = c(1, 3, 2), bty = "n", cex = 0.8, xpd = TRUE,
         inset = c(-0.62, 0), y.intersp = 1.8)
}
```

| 6. Wrap and discussion | BOARD | ~5 min |

- **As taught (Oct. 26):** framing opened with validation and CV as the
  gold standard, then LRT and AIC as single-fit shortcuts. Coverage not
  yet reported.
- R = Monday section of `CODE_Week10_ModelComparison.R`. No Stan debrief (lab).
- **Behind?** Skip the Poisson pause and AICc/BIC; past minute ~38, do

# Part 1: Lecture content

## 1. Big picture (~4 min) [BOARD]

```{r workflow-fig, fig.width=6.5, fig.height=2.6, dev="png", dpi=250}
draw_workflow("COMPARE")
```

- COMPARE = fit / prediction and rivals / relevance; today is the middle one
- Gold standard: predict new data from the same process (validation; CV
  when no new data). Brief; CV in depth later
- Shortcuts from one fit: LRT (nested test), AIC (estimates
  out-of-sample prediction; ~ leave-one-out CV in large samples)
- Ridge, lasso: fit skeptically; $\lambda$ usually by CV
- Survivors are corroborated, not proven

## 2. WOD: bias-variance tradeoff (~8 min) [handout]

```{r wod-fig, fig.width=4.5, fig.height=2.4}
draw_wod()
```

- Residual SS: line `r f1(sum(resid(wod_line)^2))`, curve 0
- New plot **14 cm**; line `r f1(wod_pred["line"])`, curve `r f1(wod_pred["curve"])`
- Land: in-sample fit always improves with flexibility

## 3. Likelihood ratio test (~8 min) [BOARD $\to$ R]

- Fir (Bolker 6.6): cones $\sim \text{NegBin}(a\,\text{DBH}^b, k)$; full
  (wave/non-wave $a, b, k$; 6 params) vs. no-wave (3)
- $D = 2(\text{NLL}_{red} - \text{NLL}_{full}) \sim \chi^2_r$; nested models only
- Week 7's 1.92 = this test with $r = 1$

```{r chisq-fig, fig.width=4.5, fig.height=2.2}
draw_chisq()
```

- **Result:** $D = `r f2(lrt_dev)`$, $p = `r f2(lrt_p)`$; keep no-wave
- **Pause:** Poisson nested in NB? Yes ($k \to \infty$; legacy LECTURE8
  is wrong), but on the boundary, so naive $p$ is ~2x too big.
  $D =$ `r format(round(pois_dev), big.mark = ",")` here
- **Sticking point:** not rejecting $\neq$ no difference

## 4. AIC (~10 min) [BOARD $\to$ R]

- $\text{AIC} = -2\log\mathcal{L}(\hat\theta) + 2k$; nested or not, same response data
- $2k$ = average in-sample optimism (`NOTES_Reference_AICPenalty.Rmd`; don't derive)
- $w_i = e^{-\Delta_i/2}/\sum_j e^{-\Delta_j/2}$; BIC: $k \log n$

```{r aic-table}
tab_show <- aic_tab[, c("k", "nll", "AIC", "dAIC", "weight", "BIC")]
tab_show$BIC <- bic_d
names(tab_show) <- c("k", "NLL", "AIC", "dAIC", "weight", "dBIC")
rownames(tab_show) <- gsub("_", "\\\\_", rownames(tab_show))
# latex tabular (not longtable) so the table can't split across pages
show_aic <- function() {
  knitr::kable(tab_show, format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE,
               digits = c(0, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2))
}
show_aic()
```

- **Pause:** weight `r f2(aic_tab["no_wave", "weight"])` = P(true model)?
  No; relative support within the set (Bolker p. 284)
- **Sticking point:** `const_ak` adds 1 param, NLL down only
  `r f2(fit_nowave$value - fit_constak$value)`, yet $\Delta$ =
  `r f2(aic_tab["const_ak", "dAIC"])`. A useless parameter costs $\le 2$
  (Arnold 2010)

## 5. Ridge and lasso (~12 min) [BOARD $\to$ R]

- Creepers: 50 stations, 10 covariates, simulated (say so); truth =
  big trees, snags, road distance
- $2^{10} = 1024$ subsets; instead penalize coefficient *size*:
  $\text{NLL} + \lambda\sum\beta_j^2$ (ridge), $\text{NLL} + \lambda\sum|\beta_j|$ (lasso)
- Standardize first; $\lambda$ by 10-fold CV (`lambda.1se`)
- Lasso's corner at 0 gives exact zeros:

```{r penalty-fig, fig.width=4.5, fig.height=2.4}
draw_penalty_1d()
```

- **Full MLE:** all 10 nonzero; north `r f2(b_mle["north"])`, elev `r f2(b_mle["elev"])` (truth 0)
- **All-subsets AIC:** `r lst(best_set)`; `r n_within2` within 2; best weight `r f2(best_wt)`
- **Top-models table:** the true model ranks `r true_rank` ($\Delta$AIC
  `r f2(true_daic)`). `r sum(plus_one)` of the next 9 are the best model
  plus one covariate, at $\Delta$AIC `r f2(min(plus_one_daic))` to
  `r f2(max(plus_one_daic))`: uninformative parameters (section 4, Arnold
  2010). Pause: which covariates are in nearly every top model?
- **Lasso (CV):** `r lst(lasso_set)`; big trees `r f2(b_lasso["big_trees"])` (truth 0.5), road `r f2(b_lasso["road_dist"])` (0.3)
- **Ridge (CV, same folds and rule):** no zeros, everything shrunk hard:
  big trees `r f2(b_ridge["big_trees"])`, snags `r f2(b_ridge["snags"])`,
  road `r f2(b_ridge["road_dist"])`, north `r f2(b_ridge["north"])`. At
  `lambda.min` much less: big trees `r f2(b_ridge_min["big_trees"])`,
  road `r f2(b_ridge_min["road_dist"])`, north `r f2(b_ridge_min["north"])`
  (mention only if asked)
- **40 simulated datasets**, exact true set: AIC `r n_aic_right`, lasso `r n_lasso_right`

- **Pause:** road `r f2(b_lasso["road_dist"])` vs. 0.3, broken? No:
  bias traded for lower variance; for effect sizes refit or go Bayesian (Wed.)
- **Sticking point:** neither method is a truth detector

## 6. Wrap and discussion (~5 min) [BOARD]

- Count penalty / held-out data / size penalty. Tomorrow: pond survey.
  Wed.: WAIC, LOO, shrinkage priors

**Q1.** AIC kept northness (`r n_within2` models within 2, best weight
`r f2(best_wt)`); the lasso dropped it. Which covariates would you
report as "important," and how would you word it?

**Q2.** In a real survey, the lasso sets grazing to exactly 0. A manager
concludes expanding grazing won't affect creepers. Agree?

- Q1 lands on: report selection uncertainty; agreed covariates (big
  trees, snags) are safest
- Q2 lands on: zero = not needed for prediction here, not "no effect";
  grazing may act via shrub cover; causal question = COMPARE (3), relevance

# PART 2: PODIUM CHEAT SHEET

\normalsize
\textit{Tight on purpose. Detail: Part 1. R = Monday section of CODE\_Week10\_ModelComparison.R.}
\large

**Order:** big picture $\to$ WOD $\to$ lecture (no Stan debrief; that's at lab). **Behind?** Skip the Poisson pause and the AICc/BIC columns; move the glmnet demo to Wednesday.

## 1. Big picture (~4 min) [BOARD]

```{r podium-workflow, fig.width=6.5, fig.height=2.6, dev="png", dpi=250}
draw_workflow("COMPARE")
```

- Point at **COMPARE**: (1) does it fit, (2) does it beat its rivals and predict new data, (3) is it relevant to the problem
- Weeks 6-9 were FIT; today is (2): which models do the data support?
- Toughest test: how well does the model predict **new data from the same process**? Validation (score on data it never saw); cross-validation when there are no new data (hold out, fit, score, rotate; in depth later)
- CV means fitting many times. Shortcuts from a single fit: LRT (does the bigger nested model beat chance?) and AIC (estimates out-of-sample prediction; ranks like leave-one-out CV in large samples)
- Third route: fit one big model skeptically (ridge, lasso), with the penalty usually tuned by CV
- Survivors are corroborated, not proven
- Hand out the WOD

\newpage

## 2. WOD: bias-variance tradeoff (~8 min)

```{r podium-wod, fig.width=4.5, fig.height=2.6}
draw_wod()
```

- Sum of squared residuals: line `r f1(sum(resid(wod_line)^2))`, curve 0. The curve "wins" on the data it was fit to
- New plot measured **14 cm**. Line predicted `r f1(wod_pred["line"])`; this curve `r f1(wod_pred["curve"])`
- Compare neighbors: curves disagree in the gap, lines don't
- **Land:** in-sample fit always improves as a model gets more flexible, so we need a penalty or new data

\newpage

## 3. Likelihood ratio test (~8 min) [BOARD $\to$ R]

- Fir cones $\sim$ NegBin(mean $a\,\text{DBH}^b$, dispersion $k$). Do wave sites differ?
- Full: separate $a, b, k$ for wave and non-wave (6 params). Reduced: one set (3). Reduced is a special case of full: **nested**
- Deviance $D = 2(\text{NLL}_{red} - \text{NLL}_{full}) \sim \chi^2_r$, $r$ = params fixed
- Callback: Week 7's 1.92 cutoff = this test with $r = 1$ (3.84/2)

```{r podium-chisq, fig.width=4.5, fig.height=2.2}
draw_chisq()
```

- **R:** $D = `r f2(lrt_dev)`$ vs. cutoff 7.81 ($p = `r f2(lrt_p)`$): keep the simpler no-wave model
- **Pause (skippable):** "Is the Poisson model nested in the negative binomial? Can we use an LRT?" *Land:* yes, nested ($k \to \infty$), but $k = \infty$ is on the boundary, so the naive $p$ is about twice too big. Here $D =$ `r format(round(pois_dev), big.mark = ",")`, so it doesn't matter
- **Sticking point:** not rejecting $\neq$ "wave and non-wave trees are the same"; 242 trees just can't tell them apart

\newpage

## 4. AIC (~10 min) [BOARD $\to$ R]

- $\text{AIC} = -2\log\mathcal{L}(\hat\theta) + 2k$: ranks any models fit to the same response, nested or not
- $2k$ = average optimism of in-sample fit (the WOD's curve, in one number); don't derive
- $\Delta_i = \text{AIC}_i - \text{AIC}_{min}$; weights $w_i = e^{-\Delta_i/2} / \sum_j e^{-\Delta_j/2}$
- AICc: small-sample correction. BIC: $k \log n$ in place of $2k$ (harsher)

```{r podium-aic}
show_aic()
```

- **Pause:** "The no-wave model has weight `r f2(aic_tab["no_wave", "weight"])`. Is there a `r round(100 * aic_tab["no_wave", "weight"])`% chance it's the true model?" *Land:* no; relative support within this set, not a probability (Bolker p. 284)
- **Sticking point:** `const_ak` adds 1 param, NLL drops only `r f2(fit_nowave$value - fit_constak$value)`, yet it's only `r f2(aic_tab["const_ak", "dAIC"])` behind. A useless parameter costs at most 2, so "within 2" $\neq$ support (Arnold 2010)

\newpage

## 5. Ridge and lasso (~12 min) [BOARD $\to$ R]

- Creepers: 50 point counts, 10 standardized habitat covariates. **Simulated, so we know the truth:** big trees, snags, road distance
- $2^{10} = 1024$ subsets. Instead, keep all 10 and penalize coefficient *size*: $\text{NLL} + \lambda\sum\beta_j^2$ (ridge), $\text{NLL} + \lambda\sum|\beta_j|$ (lasso)
- AIC penalizes how many; these penalize how big. Standardize first

```{r podium-penalty, fig.width=4.5, fig.height=2.4}
draw_penalty_1d()
```

- Lasso's corner at 0 gives exact zeros; ridge only shrinks
- **R, MLE:** all 10 nonzero; northness `r f2(b_mle["north"])`, elevation `r f2(b_mle["elev"])` (both truly 0)
- **R, all-subsets AIC:** best = `r lst(best_set)` (north spurious); `r n_within2` models within 2; top weight only `r f2(best_wt)`
- **R, top-models table:** truth ranks `r true_rank` ($\Delta$AIC `r f2(true_daic)`); `r sum(plus_one)` of the next 9 = best model + one useless covariate, each at $\Delta \approx 2$. **Pause:** "Which covariates show up in nearly every top model?" *Land:* big trees, snags, road; the rest come and go
- **R, CV lasso** (`lambda.1se`): keeps `r lst(lasso_set)`, zeroes the rest
- **R, CV ridge** (same folds): no zeros; big trees `r f2(b_ridge["big_trees"])`, road `r f2(b_ridge["road_dist"])`
- **Pause:** "The lasso kept road distance but says its effect is `r f2(b_lasso["road_dist"])`; the truth is 0.3. Is the lasso broken?" *Land:* no. Shrinkage is the point: biased, less noisy estimates that predict better. Good for prediction and choosing covariates, not for effect sizes (refit, or Bayesian on Wednesday)
- Across 40 simulated datasets, exact true set: AIC `r n_aic_right`, lasso `r n_lasso_right`. Neither is a truth detector

\newpage

## 6. Wrap and discussion (~5 min)

- Three ways to compare: penalize the count (LRT, AIC), test on held-out data (CV), penalize the size (ridge, lasso)
- Tomorrow: the pond survey. Wednesday: Bayesian versions (WAIC, LOO, shrinkage priors)

**Q1.** AIC's best creeper model kept northness (`r n_within2` models within 2 units; top weight `r f2(best_wt)`); the lasso dropped it. Which covariates would you report as "important," and how would you word it?

- *Land:* report the uncertainty, not one list; covariates both methods agree on (big trees, snags) are the safest claims

**Q2.** In a real survey, the lasso sets grazing to exactly 0. A manager concludes expanding grazing won't affect creepers. Agree?

- *Land:* a zero means "not needed to predict counts here," not "no effect"
- Grazing may act through shrub cover, or be real but too small for 50 stations. A management question is causal: COMPARE (3), relevance
